Symptoms: fever, headache, mild diarrhea, later dizziness, tachycardia, tachypnoea, clinical deterioration
Death_cause: Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) and respiratory failure
Travel_comment: Epidemiological investigations traced the travel history of the first two cases, a couple who had spent approximately five months birdwatching across South America. They also visited a municipal landfill located approximately four miles outside Ushuaia known for birdwatching.
Confirmation_comment: Early sequencing of ANDV from the patients showed a high degree of similarity to previously reported sequences from Argentina. An initial zoonotic introduction before the departure of the ship from Argentina on April 1 is likely, because symptoms developed in Patient 1 on April 6, and he had a 3-month travel history to regions with known enzootic circulation of ANDV. No samples were available from this patient.

Death_cause: pneumonia and Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Travel_comment: Epidemiological investigations traced the travel history of the first two cases, a couple who had spent approximately five months birdwatching across South America. They also visited a municipal landfill located approximately four miles outside Ushuaia known for birdwatching. On April 25, Case 2 took the flight from Saint Helena to Johannesburg (Airlink flight 4Z 132). The airlink flight was carrying 82 passengers and six crew. She then intended to travel by air on a connecting flight to the Netherlands via Johannesburg, South Africa [KLM592], carrying 82 passengers and six crew members but she was deemed too ill and was offloaded before takeoff.
Confirmation_comment: Laboratory testing performed at the National Institute for Communicable Diseases in South Africa (NICD) confirmed Hantavirus infection on 4 May. Sequencing of samples from the subsequent patients showed a high level of genetic similarity, with a maximum of one detected single-nucleotide polymorphism per patient. Further epidemiologic analysis is needed to determine whether this outbreak resulted from one or more zoonotic spillover events or from human-to-human transmission

Symptoms: fever, shortness of breath, signs of pneumonia, condition worsened, presented in shock and with Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS)
Contact_comment: The case had accommodation located two cabins away from Cases 1 and 2; therefore, onboard exposure is likely. Epidemiological investigation further revealed that Case 3 had also been in Argentina from 18 March 2026 and had participated in remote birdwatching activities prior to boarding the vessel on 1 April
Travel_comment: The case was medically evacuated to South Africa on 2026-04-27
Confirmation_comment: samples from Patient 3 were sent to the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD) in South Africa, where the diagnosis was confirmed on May 2 by pan-hantavirus reverse-transcriptase polymerase-chain-reaction (RT-PCR) assay. sequencing of the L segment from Patients 2 and 3 at the NICD confirmed the presence of Andes virus (ANDV) on May 5. Viral genetic sequencing results are nearly identical to those of Case 2.
Antemortem samples were sent from Cabo Verde for testing at the Institut Pasteur de Dakar, where hantavirus infection was confirmed on 8 May 2026.

Contact_comment: Cruise passenger, disembarked at Saint Helena.
Travel_comment: He had arrived in Argentina one week prior to embarking on the cruise vessel. After disembarkation (mid-voyage) in Saint Helena on 22 April, while asymptomatic, he subsequently travelled with his wife on a commercial flight back to Switzerland on 27 and 28 April.
Confirmation_comment: Laboratory testing confirmed PCR positivity for Andes virus on 5 May 2026.

Contact_comment: The case had possible onboard exposure through close occupational contact with other confirmed cases in his role as an expedition guide.
Confirmation_comment: Tested positive by PCR and sequencing for ANDV on May 8

Contact_comment: The case is the second positive case among the 14 Spanish nationals who were evacuated from Tenerife. The case corresponds to a close contact identified within the epidemiological follow-up activated after the initial detection of the outbreak. The affected person was one of the individuals remaining in preventive quarantine at Gomez Ulla Hospital, and had been under clinical surveillance and isolation since their admission. Following confirmation, the patient was transferred to the High-Level Isolation Unit of Gomez Ulla Hospital.
